citation.title: Designing a TPMS metamaterial via deep learning and topology optimization
citation.authors: Asha Viswanath, Diab W. Abueidda, Mohamad Modrek, Rashid K. Abu Al-Rub, Seid Koric, Kamran A. Khan

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: One conventional 3D topology-optimization example takes 2.4 hours on an HPC core, whereas a trained CNN prediction takes 0.001 CPU hour.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: [inferred] Section 3.2 states 2.4 h per classical data-point run; Table 2 gives 0.001 CPU h per DL prediction. 2.4/0.001 = 2400, across different computing setups.
claim.alternatives: Abstract says prediction is instantaneous; introduction states about 67 s per classical iteration and about 200–800 iterations; conclusion repeats nearly instant prediction.

baseline.classical_method: 3D homogenization-based density SIMP topology optimization, maximizing bulk or shear modulus (Section 2.2)
baseline.implementation: Modified Gao et al. MATLAB 3D TO code (Section 2.2)
baseline.hardware_classical: IBM HPC: two 12-core Intel Xeon E5-2695 v2 CPUs, two NVIDIA K20M GPUs, 264 GB RAM; iForge: 40-core Intel/Skylake nodes, 192 GB RAM, some NVIDIA V100 nodes (Section 3.2)
baseline.hardware_ml: HPC GPU for training; prediction described as possible on a laptop; specific prediction hardware not stated (Section 3.2)
baseline.classical_iterations: About 200–800 iterations to converge (introduction); unsuccessful cases discarded after 1,000 iterations (Section 5)
baseline.classical_time: About 67 s per iteration (introduction); 2.4 h per data-point run on one HPC core; 24 h parallel data generation (Section 3.2, Table 2)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 2,751 topology optimization data points; 2.4 h each on one HPC core; 24 h elapsed with parallel jobs (Section 3.2, Table 2)
baseline.quality_metric: MSE and Dice similarity of density images; predicted-versus-reference volume deviations (Sections 3.3, 5)
baseline.quality_gap: Test-set MSE 0.0079; mean Dice about 95%; mean volume deviation 0.24%, maximum absolute deviation 1.73% (Section 5, Figures 13–15)

R1.evidence: Abstract and Sections 3.3/5 compare inference with full TO, but assess predicted designs by image overlap and volume, not a matched physical objective or FE budget.

R2.evidence: Section 3.2/Table 2 give a one-core HPC TO runtime and a CNN prediction runtime, without matched hardware or a justification for the choice.

R3.evidence: Section 3.2/Table 2 report 2,751 optimization runs, 24 h parallel data generation and 5.5 GPU h training, but no break-even number of uses.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.3/5 use voxel MSE and Dice for output quality; predicted designs lack an FE evaluation of returned bulk/shear modulus. Section 5 notes discarded disconnected or nonconverged training designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: 5% of the final dataset used for testing; 2,597 bulk and 2,741 shear data points after exclusions (Section 5)

notes: Section 5/Figure 16 tests parameter values outside the training grid. Code URL is given in the data availability statement; public code appears runnable under the article's stated educational availability. Failure counts are supplied for classical training designs, not returned CNN designs.
